players.name: Victor
players.persona: the village constable, suspicious by nature

players.name: Mary
players.persona: the baker, who knows everything about everyone

players.name: Jasper
players.persona: the blacksmith, few words but blunt

thought: First night, no information yet. Pick someone sharp and likely to lead the village. Victor talks a lot, he'll steer suspicion. Better to silence him early.
say: Jasper, dear, I say we take Victor tonight. He's the loudest voice in Mistmoor, always organizing, always pointing fingers. If he's the seer, we're done for; if he's not, we still lose the village's natural leader. Either way, fewer speeches to sit through tomorrow. What do you think?

thought: Victor talks too much and watches too closely. Mary is right, and I want her to trust my judgment tonight.
say: Victor, then. He's the one everyone listens to, and the one who'd unmask us first. Hit the head and the rest of the village goes quiet. Agreed?

thought: Jasper agrees. Victor it is. Tomorrow I bake bread and wring my hands with the best of them.
Victor it is. Mary and I agree, and the village loses its loudest voice before dawn.
Victor is the victim. Saving him on night 1 is a fair gamble, since I know nothing yet. I'll keep the poison until I have a real suspect.
Night falls, and I still have my nose for liars. Let's see what that smooth-talking Victor is really hiding behind his grin.
No death on night one. Either the witch saved someone or the wolves slipped. I know nothing yet, so I watch who stays too quiet.
say: Nobody died, folks. Either the witch is awake and generous, or the wolves fumbled. Constable's rule: trust nobody, and I mean it warmly. I'll be watching who gets too chatty and who gets too quiet. Speak up, everyone, silence smells suspicious to me.

thought: Victor knows he was saved? No, he only guesses. Stay chatty, keep my role hidden, and watch who pushes hardest for suspicion.
say: Well, my friends, an innkeeper loves a quiet morning, and nobody dead is the best breakfast news! Maybe the witch is generous, maybe the wolves have bad aim. Victor, you want chatty? I'm chatty by trade, so suspect my stories, not my silence. Who else has thoughts?

thought: Victor is clean. I shouldn't reveal myself yet. Keep it touchy and observant, steer attention toward quiet folks without exposing my role.
say: Well, as your former mayor, and yes, I still remember the keys to the town hall, I say a quiet night is no reason to relax. Victor talks like a constable should, fine by me. Owen, your stories are long but honest-sounding. It's Hugo, Mary, Iris, Rose and Jasper I want to hear. Don't make me ask twice!

thought: Nobody dead, thank the saints. I know nothing yet. Best keep my head down, sound honest, and watch who pushes hardest without reason.
say: A quiet night, and I crossed myself three times for it. I'm just a shepherd, I know sheep better than wolves, but sheep teach you one thing: the flock scatters when something smells wrong. Nothing smells wrong yet. Leo, you're quick to hand out marks, like you're still grading us. I'll listen before I point.

thought: The witch saved Victor. Annoying, but it tells me the witch exists and wasted her potion. Now I smile, knead dough, and point softly elsewhere.
say: Nobody died, and my bread still rose, so I call it a good morning. But listen: whoever the wolves bit, the witch saved them. That means somebody at this table knows exactly who's safe. Leo, you dish out orders like the keys still work. Hugo, you're awfully humble for a man who counts sheep by sniffing wolves. I'm watching both.

thought: Everyone is talking and nobody has said anything juicy yet. Mary's bread theory is clever, though. I'll listen to Rose and Jasper before I commit to anyone.
say: Good morning, Mistmoor! I sew for half of you, so I hear everything, and I've heard nothing suspicious yet. Mary, if the witch saved someone, that's a secret worth a whole bolt of gossip. Rose, Jasper, you've been quiet. Tell me something, anything, before I start stitching theories together.

thought: I know nothing more than anyone. Mary's point about the witch is clever, maybe too clever? Leo is bossy but seems sincere. I'll stay friendly and watch.
say: Good morning, everyone! My mill wheel creaked all night, but no screams, thank goodness. I'm just a miller, I trust folks too easily, I know. Mary, you seemed very keen to point out that someone knows who's safe. Why poke the witch so early? Leo, Hugo, you both seem honest enough. Jasper, your turn, dear, don't be shy!

thought: Victor survived, so the witch must have saved him. Mary is pointing at the witch; I should back a neutral line and keep my head down.
say: Nothing to say, really. Nobody died, so somebody's luck held or somebody's potion did. I'll watch who talks too much, Leo, and who talks too little. Hugo's sheep, Iris's gossip, I'll hear them all before I swing a hammer at anyone.

thought: Mary's witch remark is odd, but it could be plain logic. Rose pounced on her fast. Jasper said almost nothing. No real evidence yet, so I vote cautiously.
say: Rose, you pounced on Mary fast, but Mary only said what any baker could figure. Odd, yes, but not wolfish. Jasper, 'nothing to say' is the shortest speech yet, and I did warn about silence. Leo, you handed out orders, but that's mayor habit. Jasper, give me one real opinion.

thought: Mary guessing the witch is risky for me, but she may just be clever. Rose pouncing on her is interesting. Jasper is vague. Keep suspicion light and avoid revealing myself.
say: Easy now, Mary's right that someone's potion may have worked, but I'd not hang a baker for arithmetic. Rose, you jumped on her quick, though I'll allow millers get nervous. Jasper, Victor's right, give us one real opinion. A hammer swings better with an aim, my friend!

thought: Hugo and Mary both jabbed at me, touchy indeed. Jasper is evasive. Rose deflected quickly. I'll press Jasper without revealing anything.
say: Grading you, Hugo? Hmph. Someone has to keep order, and I'll thank you both to notice I asked questions, not handed out nooses. Now, Jasper: you watch, you listen, you say nothing. That's either wisdom or a wolf waiting for dark. Rose, you jumped on Mary rather quickly too. Jasper, one real opinion, or my vote leans your way.

thought: Everyone piles on Jasper, and that makes me twitchy. Wolves love a herd running one way. Rose's quick pounce on Mary itched me more.
say: Here's my real opinion, Leo, since you're counting. Jasper's a blank page, but a blank page isn't a wolf, just a lazy one. What itched me was Rose: Mary said plain sense and Rose pounced like a dog on a dropped sausage. When the whole flock runs one way, I check what's chasing from behind. My vote leans Rose, lightly.

thought: Rose pounced on me, lucky for us. Steer the vote her way, nudge Jasper to talk, and look like a baker defending her honor, nothing more.
say: Well, Rose, I'll take 'why poke the witch' as a compliment to my arithmetic. Jasper, say something, dear, the village needs a sentence from you, not a shrug. But a quiet man isn't a wolf; a loud accusation at a baker who stated the obvious, that's what makes my dough sink. My vote leans Rose, and I say it kindly.

thought: Rose jumped on Mary fast, and Hugo and Mary both lean her way now. Jasper says almost nothing, but he's not the one I'd bet on. I'd rather watch Rose a little longer.
say: Oh, this village is a bolt of mismatched cloth! Rose, you did rush at Mary, and I'll admit it looked odd. But Jasper hasn't given us a single real thought, and a silent man deserves more than a shrug from me. Jasper, speak properly, dear, or I'll be stitching you into my next theory. I'm not voting yet.

thought: Oh dear, everyone's piling on me. I only asked a question. Hugo and Mary leaned in fast. Jasper's silence still worries me most.
say: Goodness, I asked Mary one question and suddenly I'm the sausage! Fair enough, Mary, it was plain arithmetic, I'm sorry for poking. But Hugo and Mary both leaned my way rather quickly for a light suspicion. Meanwhile Jasper has given us one shrug and a hammer. I'd rather hear him properly. My vote goes to Jasper unless he finally speaks up.

thought: Mary is steering the vote onto Rose, and everyone wants me to speak. I must sound useful without drawing fire. Rose is an honest mark for now.
say: Fine, a real opinion. Rose pounced on Mary, that's fair. But Hugo and Mary both piled on Rose in one breath, and that's too neat for me. Leo asks questions, Victor warns about silence, Iris stitches theories. I'll vote with my hammer, not my mouth, and I'm watching who keeps the pile growing.

thought: Rose pounced on Mary, then Hugo and Mary piled on her, and Rose now threatens Jasper. Jasper stayed vague. Tough call, but Rose's early push was the oddest move, and the votes lean her way.
Rose pounced on Mary, then wavered and now points at Jasper. Jasper stayed vague. Rose seems the likeliest wolf, and Hugo and Mary both lean her way. I'll vote Rose.
Jasper finally spoke, but his words are vague. Rose rushed Mary, yet Hugo and Mary piling onto her together feels coordinated. Jasper stays evasive, so my vote goes to him.
Rose apologized and turned it on me and Mary neatly. Jasper still says nothing real. My gut says Rose, but my hand shakes. Stick with it.
I said Rose, Hugo said Rose. Stay consistent, keep my hands floury and clean. Jasper, don't vote with me, it looks like a pair.

Rose and Jasper are both now pointing at each other, and Hugo and Mary keep piling onto Rose. I don't trust that pile. Jasper's speech was thin, but Rose has been jumping at everyone, so I'll lean toward the one who pushes hardest.
Jasper finally spoke, and he noticed the same neat pile I did. Hugo started it, and Mary followed. I'll vote Hugo and hope I'm right.
Rose is the easy mark, and the pile already leans her way. Voting with it keeps Mary safe and keeps my hands clean.
Well, that's that. A plain miller gone. I hope they catch the real wolves. Hugo and Mary still feel off to me.
say: Well, flour to flour, dust to dust! I was just a plain miller, friends, as the reveal shows. Remember who started the pile: Hugo leaned first, Mary followed close behind. And Jasper, you called the pile too neat, then joined it anyway. Watch those three closely. Take care of my mill wheel, and catch those wolves!

thought: Leo already voted Jasper and he's the loudest after Victor. Hugo must stay alive, he's our lovely scapegoat. Take Leo and let Rose's words point at Hugo.
say: Jasper, Leo tonight. He's the only one who voted against you, and he's got mayor's lungs: he'll keep hammering you tomorrow. Hugo we leave breathing, Rose's dying words put him first in line, bless her. Victor already got his potion, so the witch can't save Leo. Clean and quiet. Agreed?

thought: Leo is the one who went after me. Mary's reasons are sound, and Hugo would only sniff closer if we hit him now.
say: Leo, then. He voted against me and he talks like he already owns the town hall. Hugo can wait, he's sniffing but not yet close. Clean, quiet, and it buys us tomorrow. Agreed?

thought: Leo it is. Tomorrow the village mourns its mayor, and I point gently at Hugo, who leaned first on poor Rose.
Leo it is. Mary agrees, and the mayor's voice goes silent before tomorrow's vote.
Rose was a villager, sadly. Leo falls tonight and I can't save him. Hugo and Mary led the pile, but that's thin evidence. Better hold my poison until I have something firmer.
Poor Rose, an innocent miller. Hugo led the pile on her. If anyone steered us wrong, it was him. Tonight I check the shepherd.
Leo the seer is dead, and he was the only one to vote Jasper. That's my best lead. Hugo started the Rose pile too. I keep my poison for now, but I'll steer toward Jasper.
say: Poor Leo, the seer, gone. Wolves don't kill the loud one for fun. Notice he was the only one who voted Jasper yesterday, and Jasper gave us hammers and riddles. Hugo, you started the Rose pile, so I'm watching you too. But Jasper, tell us plainly: who do you suspect, and why?

thought: I got Rose hanged. A villager. My hands won't stop shaking. Leo saw something, and the wolves shut his eyes. Jasper joined the pile after sneering at it.
say: I'll say it plain: I pushed Rose and I was wrong, and I'll carry that like a dead lamb on my shoulders. But Leo was the seer, and the only man Leo pointed at was Jasper. Then Jasper called the pile too neat and jumped on it anyway. Owen, you're quick to name me, fine, I'll earn it back. Jasper first.

thought: Leo's vote wasn't seer knowledge, or he'd have shouted it. I must say that calmly, not fiercely, or I'm wearing Jasper's collar in front of everyone.
say: Think, friends. If Leo had seen Jasper as a wolf, he'd have shouted it from the town hall steps, not 'leaned' over a shrug. He voted on silence, nothing more. So his real check cleared somebody, and that somebody is sitting quiet, letting Jasper take the heat. Hugo, you confessed prettily, but you lit the Rose fire. I'm watching you and Owen.

thought: Leo the seer is dead, and I can't prove his last check. Hugo and Mary both pushed Rose, and Rose was innocent. Owen and Hugo are bickering, but Mary's logic is sharp. I'll keep my suspicions close until I know more.
say: Oh, poor Leo, and poor Mistmoor! I'm rattled, friends, because I was the one who gossiped about Rose's pile. Mary, you're right that Leo shouldn't have been silent about his check, but Hugo's confession counts for something. I still think Jasper's silence stinks of trouble. Let's not hang anyone on guesses today, please. Who here truly saw something last night?

thought: Leo was the seer and he died. Mary is steering suspicion toward me and Owen. I need to sound plain and not defensive, and keep Mary clear.
say: Plain, then. I voted with the pile on Rose, and I'll own that. Leo's death is a loss, and I won't pretend otherwise. Hugo confessed, which I respect. Owen and Mary both want names, so here's mine: watch who pushes hardest to hang someone, and ask why Mary defends Jasper's silence so warmly. I'm not dancing, I'm listening.

thought: Leo alone voted Jasper, and the wolves killed Leo that night. Jasper also talked about himself in the third person, which is a slip. Mary's theory is clever, but I lean Jasper.
say: Constable's notes. Leo was the only one to vote Jasper, and the wolves silenced Leo that very night. Jasper, you said 'Mary defends Jasper's silence.' Jasper is you. Odd slip. Mary's theory is tidy, but tidy isn't guilty. Hugo owned his mistake, which I respect. Jasper, answer me: why Rose?

thought: Jasper's slip about himself is the best lead I have. Mary's theory oddly shields him, but I'll keep her as a second suspect. The poison stays ready if Jasper turns out to be a wolf.
say: Victor's catch is the juiciest thing said all morning. Jasper, you answered 'why Rose' with 'I followed the pile' and then pointed at Mary for defending you, which she kind of did. Mary, I'll ask nicely: why so sure Leo cleared somebody? Today, my hammer leans Jasper.

thought: Jasper speaking of himself like a stranger, that chilled me. Mary's tidy theory shields him and points at me. Wolves travel in pairs. Jasper today, Mary I'll watch.
say: Jasper, a man who talks about Jasper like he's some fellow down the road, that's a man forgetting which skin he's wearing. And Mary, you built a whole cathedral on Leo clearing somebody, then aimed it straight at me and Owen. Tidy, like Victor said. I don't trust tidy. My vote goes Jasper, and if he comes up wolf, Mary, we'll have words.

thought: He's sinking, and he grabbed at my apron on the way down. I can't pull him out. Let go, or we both drown. Forgive me, Jasper.
say: Well, that's gratitude for you. I ask a man to speak, and he repays me by pointing at my apron. Fine, Jasper, you've convinced me, though not the way you meant. Talking about yourself like a stranger down the road is a slip I can't bake over. Hugo, you'll have your words; I'll even bring buns. My vote goes Jasper today.

thought: Jasper's slip about himself as a stranger is real, and Victor caught it. Mary and Hugo are both hammering Jasper now. Owen seems sincere. I'm leaning Jasper too, but I'd like one more word from him first.
say: Jasper, you really did talk about yourself in the third person, and Victor's catch stung for a reason. Mary, Hugo, and Owen all point at him now, and I've begun to agree. Still, I'd like one plain answer from Jasper before the vote. Why did you say Mary defends your silence, when you were the one who stayed silent?

thought: Victor caught my slip and the pile is swinging onto me. Mary voted me too, so I must not look like I'm pleading. I can name Victor's stale point and steer toward Owen.
say: Slip, yes, I wrote my own name where a stranger's should be, and I'll own it. Victor, you'd like one nervous man to hang, and I'm not him. Owen, your hammer is quick today. Hugo and Mary piled on fast, that's all I've said. Vote how you like, I'll not beg.

thought: Everyone now piles on Jasper, and I started it. Too neat again? Jasper's slip still feels real, and Leo's vote plus his death backs it. I stay on Jasper.
say: Jasper, you admit the slip but call it nerves. Fair, nerves are real. Yet Leo named you and Leo is dead. That's my whole case, no fancy cathedral. Everyone's leaning your way, so give us one thing a villager would say. Otherwise, my vote is Jasper, and I'll sleep fine.

thought: Leo voted Jasper, then died that night, and Jasper slipped into the third person. Everyone leans his way. I'll stay with my case and vote Jasper.
Everyone is converging on Jasper, and he does smell like a wolf with that slip. I'll vote him and keep my poison for later, in case he turns out to be a villager.
Everyone leans Jasper, same as everyone leaned Rose. That frightens me. But the slip and Leo's vote are all I have. Lord, let me be right this time.
Six against one, nothing saves him now. Better I vote with the village than stand beside him. Tonight I'll be the only wolf, and the loneliest baker.
Jasper's slip and Leo's dying suspicion point at him, and his answers were thin. Hugo and Mary have pushed hard, but Jasper is the one with the most cracks. I'll vote Jasper.

Mary and Hugo piled onto me, and Victor says I'm the one to hang. Hugo confessed and is not as dangerous as the rest. Mary is my partner, so I cannot vote her. Hugo carries the Rose fire and takes this vote.
Mary, you were always the better liar. Trust nobody, and carry the pack alone.
say: Well, the village got its wolf after all, just not the one it wanted. I'm the blacksmith, I hammered out what I could. Mary, you've been warm all game, so keep your buns warm too. Watch Victor's constable notes and Iris's stitches, they'll bite next. Good luck, Mistmoor.

thought: Hugo promised me words if Jasper came up wolf. He did. I'd rather not have that conversation. Sheep don't bite, but shepherds remember.
One wolf is likely left among Victor, Mary and Iris. A blind poison is a one in three gamble and a miss could cost the game. I'll hold it and listen at dawn.
Hugo's threat hangs over me like burnt bread smoke. The only way out is to call the frame a frame, and sound like a woman with nothing to hide.
say: Well, isn't that convenient. Hugo promised me words, and the wolf ate him before breakfast, so now every eye lands on the baker. Think, friends: a wolf who wanted me gone just had to let Hugo talk. Killing him points at me too neatly. Owen, you named Hugo first yesterday, then swung to Jasper. Iris, you never vote on your own stitches. I'm looking at you two.

thought: Jasper was a werewolf, and the other wolf is still hiding. Mary is trying to paint me as a wolf to save herself. Owen has been steady, and I'll keep my eyes on Victor and Mary.
say: Oh, Mary, you can't stitch me into this one, dear! Hugo's death is a real loss, and I'm sorry for him. Jasper's reveal means we still have a wolf among us, and I'm not going to hide behind gossip. Owen, you've been steady all along. Victor, I'd like to hear your constable's notes on Mary's rush to blame me. Let's think clearly, friends.

thought: Three left, one wolf. Mary defended Jasper's silence, built the 'Leo cleared somebody' theory, then dropped him when he was doomed. That looks like a wolf distancing. Owen and Iris seem steadier.
say: Constable's notes, Iris. Mary was the first to defend Jasper's silence and the first to say Leo cleared someone, which shielded him. Then she flipped when the vote was lost. Now she blames Owen and you. A wolf cutting loose a partner looks exactly like that. Mary, why defend Jasper so warmly? My vote leans you.

thought: Mary defended Jasper early, then flipped once he was lost. Victor caught Jasper's slip, which a wolf rarely does. Iris seems soft. I'll vote Mary and keep the poison for dark.
say: Sorry, Mary, but your cathedral had a Jasper-shaped door. You pushed Leo-cleared-somebody, defended his silence, then dropped him when the vote turned. Hugo dying doesn't clear you, it just clears the wolf's calendar. Iris, I'm steady, thank you. Victor spotted Jasper's slip. Mary, my vote lands on you.

thought: Two hammers on me, and Iris is the hinge. If I can't turn her, I can at least split the vote. A tie is a loaf unburnt.
say: Victor and Owen have voted as a pair every single day, and now they chorus my name like they rehearsed it. Iris, look: whoever the wolf is, he needs one more vote today, and he's asking you for it. Jasper's dying breath pointed at Victor's notes. Constable, you wrote everyone's guilt but your own. My vote is Victor. Iris, think before you lend yours.

thought: Mary is desperate, and her attack on Victor is loud. Victor and Owen are both pointing at her, and their case is solid. Jasper was a wolf, Hugo was not. One wolf remains, and Mary fits the shape. I'll stand with Owen and Victor.
say: Mary, you keep saying Victor and Owen rehearsed this, but I've listened to every word. Your defense of Jasper's silence came first, and Hugo's death happened right after you pushed him. Victor's notes are the only sensible thing said today. I'm not handing you my vote to save your buns, Mary. My vote is with Owen and Victor.

thought: Mary is the last wolf, I'm fairly sure. Owen, Iris and I all lean her way, so one more vote ends it. I just have to keep Iris steady and not stumble.
say: Mary, you call Owen and me a rehearsed pair, but Iris just said she heard every word on her own. Jasper's last words were a wolf's trick to sow doubt, and you picked it up fast. Three of us name you. Iris, Owen, hold steady. Let's finish this today.

thought: Mary is my best read. Jasper's last words named Victor and Iris, which a dying wolf would hardly do to his partner. If Mary flips villager, I'll need the poison tonight.
say: Mary, 'rehearsed pair' is a fine line, but Iris and I reached you separately. Jasper's last words named Victor and Iris, and you leapt on Victor right after. Convenient. Nobody hang a baker lightly, but your story keeps bending. Iris, Victor, hold steady. One vote, one wolf, let's finish it.

thought: Four players remain, Jasper was a wolf, and Mary has been shifty. Owen and Iris both lean Mary too. Vote Mary and end this.
Mary defended Jasper first and flipped late. Victor and Iris both lean on her. If she's a villager, I still hold the poison for tonight. Vote Mary.
Three against one. The oven's lit and I'm the loaf. At least I'll go out consistent, pointing at the constable. Goodbye, Mistmoor, the bread was good.
Mary is the last suspect, and her defense keeps bending. Jasper was the wolf, but Mary fits the shape of a partner. I'll vote Mary and finish this.
Caught fair and square. Jasper was right about one thing: keep the buns warm. I'll go out with flour on my hands and a grin.
say: Well, there it is. The baker who knew everything about everyone, caught by the one thing she couldn't hide: her own teeth. Jasper, I'm sorry, dear, I did cut you loose. Victor, your notes were better than my cathedral. Owen, Iris, you earned your quiet mornings. The ovens are still warm. Somebody take the bread out before it burns.
